beats.narration: Inkling 2 Mini stores twenty-four layers, but runs forty-eight for every token. The lab says looping makes it better. Better at what, and at what cost?
beats.narration_text: Inkling 2 Mini stores 24 layers but runs 48 per token. (1) Read loop_config in config.json and map which layers repeat, (2) compute stored vs per-token parameters, (3) put each looping claim beside its published evidence — and say what would break it.

props.command: Inkling 2 Mini stores 24 layers but runs 48 per token. (1) Read loop_config in config.json and map which layers repeat, (2) compute stored vs per-token parameters, (3) put each looping claim beside its published evidence — and say what would break it.
output: LOOP     layers 7–18 × 3 passes → 48 runs from 24 stored
COST     26.4B stored · 3.4B one pass · 5.4B per token
CLAIMS   middle > end on 27 of 28 evals — lab-only

props.title: Inkling 2 Mini, Looped Is Better?
thesis: A 26.4B mixture-of-experts model that runs its middle 12 layers three times per token —
audited with three checks you can reuse on any open model.

roadmap.label: Read the config
roadmap.body: What is stored, and what repeats — straight from config.json.

roadmap.label: Compute the cost
roadmap.body: Memory follows what's stored; compute follows what runs per token.

roadmap.label: Check the claim
roadmap.body: Put each claim beside its evidence. Then ask what would break it.

props.source: Thinking Machines, Nov 20 2026 · HF thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini config.json

beats.narration: Step one: read the config. Twenty-four layers, each sending a token to eight of a hundred twenty-eight experts. Loop config: core start six, core end eighteen, three passes. Counting from one, layers seven to eighteen run three times. Six, plus thirty-six, plus six: forty-eight.
beats.narration_text: Step one: read the config. Twenty-four layers, each sending a token to eight of a hundred twenty-eight experts. Loop config: core start six, core end eighteen, three passes. Counting from one, layers seven to eighteen run three times. Six, plus thirty-six, plus six: forty-eight.

props.heading: 24 layers stored, 48 run per token

moves.label: STORED
moves.detail: 24 layers in 4 blocks of 6; each sends a token to 8 of 128 experts.

moves.label: READ AS
moves.detail: Config counts from 0; from 1, layers 7–18 run three times, same weights.

moves.label: COUNT
moves.detail: 6 + 12 × 3 + 6 = 48 layer applications per token, from 24 stored.

props.keepNote: No need to take the lab's word for the loop: it is written in the file.
props.source: config.json (HF thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini): num_hidden_layers · n_layers_per_attn_res_block 6 · n_routed_experts · loop_config

beats.narration: Step two: compute the cost. One pass uses three point four billion parameters, per the lab. A looped layer is attention plus eight experts, about eighty-three million. Times twelve: one billion per extra pass. Two extra passes: five point four billion.
beats.narration_text: Step two: compute the cost. One pass uses three point four billion parameters, per the lab. A looped layer is attention plus eight experts, about eighty-three million. Times twelve: one billion per extra pass. Two extra passes: five point four billion.

props.heading: Parameters used per token, pass by pass
props.exception: 3.4 + 2 × 1.0 = 5.4B — the lab's table. The one-pass 3.4B is lab-reported; the +1.0B per pass is computed from config.json.
props.source: Computed from config.json (hidden 2,304 · expert FFN 1,152 · 24 q / 8 kv heads × 128) · 3.4B, 5.4B: lab post

beats.narration: Now the tension. The lab's text says three point four billion active; its table, five point four. Which is it? Memory holds all twenty-six point four billion, about twenty gigabytes. Speed tracks five point four. Looping saves memory, not compute.

props.heading: Is it a 3.4B model or a 5.4B model?

moves.label: LABELS
moves.detail: Post text: “3.4B active”. Its own table: “5.4 activated”.

moves.label: MEMORY
moves.detail: Holds all 24 layers: 26.4B params, ≈20 GB in NVFP4 + MXFP8.

moves.label: COMPUTE
moves.detail: Runs 48 layer applications: ≈5.4B params per token.

moves.label: RULE
moves.detail: Memory → the stored count. Speed and cost → the per-token count.

props.keepNote: Looping saves memory, not compute: 24 layers stored, 48 run.
props.source: Thinking Machines, Nov 20 2026 · model card: compute per token is “higher than the active-parameter count alone suggests”

beats.narration: Step three: check the claims. The lab says looping the middle beat looping the end on twenty-seven of twenty-eight evals. Its chart agrees: the ranges don't overlap. But it's one checkpoint, at step two thousand, and the twenty-eight aren't listed.
beats.narration_text: Step three: check the claims. The lab says looping the middle beat looping the end on twenty-seven of twenty-eight evals. Its chart agrees: the ranges don't overlap. But it's one checkpoint, at step two thousand, and the twenty-eight aren't listed.

props.heading: Lab: the middle loop wins 27 of 28 evals
props.exception: The middle's worst (1.51×) still beats the end's best (1.36×). But: one checkpoint (step 2,000), three evals — and the 28 evals aren't listed.
props.source: Thinking Machines, Nov 20 2026 — chart “Compute-equivalent gain by loop position” · “27 out of 28”

beats.narration: The bigger claim: over fifty percent more compute-efficient than not looping. The evidence is one sentence, a scaling-law prediction. No curves, no run sizes, no outside replication cited.
beats.narration_text: The bigger claim: over fifty percent more compute-efficient than not looping. The evidence is one sentence, a scaling-law prediction. No curves, no run sizes, no outside replication cited.

props.heading: “Over 50% more compute-efficient”

moves.label: LAB SAYS
moves.detail: The looped model is “over 50% more compute-efficient” than a non-looped one.

moves.label: EVIDENCE
moves.detail: Unpruned test runs: no-loop cost 7.5% less; its law predicts >1.5× to match.

moves.label: NOT SHOWN
moves.detail: No loss curves or run sizes in the post; no outside replication cited.

moves.label: VERIFIED
moves.detail: The loop itself: loop_config · num_passes 3 · is_varloop false.

props.keepNote: The structure is verified. The advantage is lab-reported until someone reproduces it.
props.source: Thinking Machines, Nov 20 2026 — “Looping design” · config.json loop_config

beats.narration: What would break 'looped is better'? Facts. On the lab's variable-loop model, three passes instead of one add forty-two points on a long-context graph test, but one point on closed-book trivia. Looping adds thinking, not knowledge. And the one-pass handicap hit both.
beats.narration_text: What would break 'looped is better'? Facts. On the lab's variable-loop model, three passes instead of one add forty-two points on a long-context graph test, but one point on closed-book trivia. Looping adds thinking, not knowledge. And the one-pass handicap hit both.

props.heading: Three passes vs one: reasoning moves, recall doesn't
props.exception: Caveat: this model trained mostly at 3 passes, so 1-pass scores may understate — but trivia had the same handicap and still barely moved.
props.source: TML-d24-varloop-research model card §5 · lab: “knowledge is mostly a function of total parameter count”

beats.narration: The verdict. The loop: verified. The cost: five point four billion per token, computed. Middle beats end, and fifty percent more efficient: lab-only. Looping buys reasoning, not knowledge.

beats.narration: Your turn. Paste this. Thirty reasoning questions, thirty trivia questions, against a non-looped model with similar per-token compute. Good: it wins reasoning and ties trivia. Flag: no gain on either.
beats.narration_text: Run Inkling 2 Mini locally (Ollama, 32 GB+ Mac) beside a non-looped open model with about 5B active parameters — match per-token compute, not the 3.4B headline. Ask both 30 multi-step reasoning questions and 30 closed-book trivia questions. Report accuracy and tokens/s for each. Does looping help reasoning more than recall?

props.command: Run Inkling 2 Mini locally (Ollama, 32 GB+ Mac) beside a non-looped open model with about 5B active parameters — match per-token compute, not the 3.4B headline. Ask both 30 multi-step reasoning questions and 30 closed-book trivia questions. Report accuracy and tokens/s for each. Does looping help reasoning more than recall?
output: GOOD   wins on reasoning · ties on trivia
FLAG   no reasoning gain → the lab's claim doesn't transfer
